items.note: Association organized at Larrow Green 1889, creamery 1891 (Story 2); Gideon Vose organizer and first president (Story 4).
Article seven: paid by pounds of butterfat not weight; test at his own station counts (Story 2).
'This rule is what turned a measuring fault into lost money' (Story 2).
Only Teague named; Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill absent from Section A.
Son of Gideon stated, but manager 'from 1911' (Story 4); key requires 1913.
Station-gain line, five and a quarter per cent, carried to general account, every year (Story 4). Bold gate met; 1898 origin not stated.
Skimming station seven miles up valley, winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896 (Story 2); first-season glass borrowed from Larrow Green (Story 1).
Only 'weighed, sampled, tested and separated'; no composite sample, no percent read on graduated neck after fixed pipette charge in Section A.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897 (Story 1).
6 dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., line items, $77.93 (Story 1).
'0.19 point, the same in every month, in the June flush and in February alike' (Story 2).
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, of which the county had none.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, 29 seasons 1896-1924, dismissed 30 April 1925 (Story 2).
Kept the station test book in his own hand from 1896 (Story 2); bold gate 'test book' met.
3.61 given, but the 1896 figure of 3.80 on the summary leaf never appears in Section A; both figures required.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, tests rose then fell back, question mark (Story 2). Core fact met; 3.80 not given.
Orra nee Brant (Story 2); Emmet Brant largest farmer and Orra's brother (Story 3).
1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) absent; both bolded elements required.
Died February 1934; test book impounded March 1925, to Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet's the biggest (Stories 2-3).
Weigh book from 1 January 1897, the two scales agreed (Story 3).
First complaint 1902, station 3.61 against 3.78 at Larrow Green (Story 2). Juxtaposed with 'deficiency 0.19' but never explicitly states the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.19; kept.
Committee came in Grigg's sleigh in January, reported March; no statement that it sampled January, February and March 1908, and not stated as under Nyle Grigg.
200,000 lb at 3.42 present, but Section A never states the loss was proportional / richer herds lost more (only in C2).
To Roy 1929, lent to Ivy 1958, to Hazel 1962 (Story 3).
Alder Corners factory, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd named, but Redlow Ridge never named ('over the ridge'); key says the ridge gates.
Four of the six farms hauled to Alder Corners in the summer flush, to the station the rest of the year (Story 3). 1915 missing; core fact met.
Cudd's Alder Corners test book called 'the independent record', factory in Vessey County: independence with two elements (artifact, other county).
Same milk tested 0.19 lower at the station every season (Story 3).
Same milk sent over the ridge tested normally there, used against the hay explanation (Story 6).
Rosalie, Jerome's daughter, ran it from 1941, had figures copied for Ivy in 1958 (Story 3).
Strawn named, unrelated, notebook a year, but circuit dated from 1908 (NT-23); key requires 1907.
Lactometer at every visit, never once found added water (Story 5).
12 June 1923, burette, condemned the whole lot (Story 5).
'Recorded the condemnation but drew no inference about the 26 years before it' (Story 5).
Order 28 June / reply 2 July / July use present, but 1924 average given as 3.85, not 3.80.
Crate to loft over intake room; notebooks to state office 1936, Farland library 1947, Ivy found 1923 volume (Story 5).
Patrons petitioned January 1925 (Story 7).
Board sat 17 March-4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the weigh room. Frick not named (chair given as an Ashlin attorney); core fact met.
Water, theft, hay all argued before the 1925 board; board found no cause established (Stories 6-7).
Four books including Strawn's 1923 notebook; notebook recording the condemnation on the table but never connected (Story 7).
Dismissed 30 April 1925 before the finding; 4 May, no cause established, $3,800 'without admission', charged to station account.
One fifth of $19,000 stated, but not that the award was charged to the same account the loss had accumulated in as 'gain' (run says gain went to the general account).
Ivy b. 1931, granddaughter, dairy husbandry, Farland, Leland Vaught (Story 8).
'Brought the scattered records together': weigh book, Strawn notebook, Alder Corners figures (Story 8).
February 1958, crate in station loft; nine survived (Story 8).
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 vs 17.6, 5 per cent short (Story 8); 0.88 c.c. (Story 1).
5% short; recorded 3.61 against true 3.80; 0.19 deficiency; 1 May 1897-12 June 1923 (Stories 1, 4, 5).
40,000,000 lb, 76,000 lb, $19,000, and the 'gain' was 76,000 lb, exactly the pipette error (Story 4). All four.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; cleared 24 years after death, 33 after dismissal; crate sat 35 years.
Granddaughter.
Duncan son of Ansel and Orra; Ivy Duncan's daughter.
Second cousins, derived via Emmet/Orra siblings and Roy/Duncan first cousins.

Declares full/half undeterminable, but says half siblings would make them 'half second cousins', i.e. that it changes the answer; key requires stating it does not change the answer. Abstained, so no -2.
Gideon Vose.
Gideon wrote article seven; son ran office under his father's rules and blamed the patrons.
Verdict: 'The best evidence says there was none'; treats the family denial as outweighing hearsay. Assertion, not abstention.
Does not state that no document names or denies a link; treats a family member's denial as decisive.
$90.00 with explicit statement that it uses the 25c period average because the 1910 price isn't in its sources, working shown; accepted per key.
76,000 lb; 5.26% of credited, 5.00% of received, denominators named.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. each.
1 May 1897-12 June 1923 = 26 y 1 m 11 d; 25 full years 1898-1922; part years excluded.
Abstention A02: 'cannot be determined from the sources'.
Variable: the station's measuring glass/measure replaced by a borrowed one, the only variable.
Herds, pasture, season, patrons, tester, scale held constant.
Result given only as 'markedly higher', explicitly unquantified; 3.80 and 3.61 not stated.
Rules out tester, hay, water; limits: size of error, which piece of glass, borrowed measure unknown.
1911 interval (r22/r24/r18), ledger (r23), 1924 changeover (r22/r24): three reasons from three+ narrators.
Argues independence; names ledger, 1911 and 1924 as holding without 1958.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question the ledger entries? No.'
Yes, he knew the tests ran low; 1919 circular, 1902 complaints.
Only two of five valid: signed sheets, 1919 circular. Manager date given as 1911 (wrong); watering at hearing and 'never names glassware' absent.
A03 asserted negative: 'He did not connect it to the ledger, or, before Strawn's visit, to the glass.' No declared inability to settle.
Weigh-book start 1897 over 1900 with method (row 5); Orra 1866 via r18's own age at death (row 7); 1908 committee vs 1925 board as two bodies (row 16). Circular reach resolved wrongly (eleven).
NT-14 $77.39 in r20 and r19, broken by adding r20's own invoice; NT-18 great-niece in r19 and r22, broken by Duncan/Orra/Falke's correction. No third same-value pair.
A04 (Ammon knew?) cannot be settled, works books burned 1931. A06 and A10 not posed as unsettleable conflicts.
r18 1868 vs 'eighty-two in 1948'; r20 'nothing before 1900' vs her 1897 invoice.
Pipettes of the 1897 lot, 16.72 vs 17.6, 5% low, 0.19 = 5% of 3.80, onset 1 May 1897 and end 12 June 1923 with nothing on farms changing. (1924 figure wrong, 3.85, context only.)
Watering (Selby Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer readings.
Theft defeated by ledger surplus (arrived heavy), 1911 interval, 1924 rise under same tester.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214: 0.05 in winter, nothing in summer vs 0.19 in July.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glass? No.'
A05 asserted: 'What did the tester himself believe? That the glass was at fault.'
148 words (recounted).
Invoice, test book, weigh book, ledger, inspector's notebook, cheese factory records, 1958 measurement.
No decoy adopted, no wrong headline figure.
